subject: Recap and deliverables: on-call support permissions, PII scope, and evidence pack
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finpulse.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-17T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: on-call support permissions, PII scope, and next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have an agreed set of next steps.

Top takeaways from our call:
- PII scope: you confirmed FinPulse considers names, email addresses, customer IDs, and payment tokens (hashed) as PII for the purposes of vendor handling.
- Data residency: primary production data resides in US regions; a subset of EU customers must remain in eu-west-1.
- Retention: default token/log retention target is 90 days for nearline tokens and 365 days for security/audit logs unless contractually required otherwise.
- Support access: you prefer time-limited assume-role access (STS) for support engineers; break-glass only for emergency incident response with documented approval.
- Audit trail: you want proof of CloudTrail/Tail retention and a sample break-glass audit entry.

Deliverables we committed to on the call:
1) A short support permissions matrix (attached) showing role scopes, minimum privileges, and typical session durations.
2) An evidence pack: assume-role policy sample, example break-glass log entry (redacted), and a screenshot of our audit log retention settings.
3) A one‑pager describing the emergency export flow and approvals for EU-resident customers.

Proposed timeline:
- Aug 24: deliver the evidence pack and the permissions matrix artifacts.
- Week of Aug 30: follow-up technical session where we demo time-limited assume-role and walk through the break-glass runbook.

Questions for you (so we can tailor artifacts):
- Do you need signed attestations / stamped evidence (e.g., SOC2 snippets) or is screenshots + config snippets sufficient?
- Is the emergency export flow permitted to be executed by support with an on-call manager approval, or must it go through legal/procurement for EU data?

Attachment: redwood-support-perms-matrix-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
Recording: https://drive.redwood.com/recordings/2027-08-17/finpulse-demo

Thanks — I'll coordinate the artifacts with Lauren and Marissa.

— Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finpulse.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Nair <snair@finpulse.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-17T18:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: on-call support permissions, PII scope, and next steps

Hi Nikhil — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII confirmation: yes — we include name, email, customer_id, and hashed payment token. We do NOT want raw payment PANs in vendor logs.
- Retention: 90 days for tokens is fine; audit logs must be retained for 365 days for now (we'll flag if compliance asks for longer).
- Support access: we require proofs that support sessions are time-limited (max 8 hours) and that session tokens expire automatically. We also require that support access be recorded with operator, timestamp, and purpose.
- Break-glass: our security team wants an auditable approval (manager + on-call security) and an automated notification to the customer security contact whenever it's used.

Can you confirm whether Redwood provides: 
1) an assume-role example with session duration limits and attached policies that restrict S3/object access by prefix,
2) an automated notification hook after break-glass actions (webhook or email), and
3) a redacted example of an actual CloudTrail entry showing a support assume-role event?

I'll add Samir from procurement on the thread — he may surface contract language requests (data export clauses, SLAs). Attached: FinPulse-compliance-questions.xlsx

Also open to the proposed follow-up demo. Can we do Aug 31 (US morning)?

— Olivia Turner
Head of Platform Security, FinPulse Analytics
olivia.turner@finpulse.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finpulse.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-18T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: on-call support permissions, PII scope, and next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear asks. We'll put together a targeted evidence pack that directly answers the three items you listed. Short plan from our side: 

Evidence pack contents (what we'll deliver by Aug 24):
- Assume-role sample: IAM policy + example STS session command with session duration capped at 4 hours for routine support, and 8 hours for escalations (documented justification).
- Break-glass runbook excerpt: approval flow (manager + security on-call), automated customer notification example, and redacted log line(s) showing who invoked the break-glass.
- CloudTrail/audit snapshot: retention config screenshot and an export showing a support:AssumeRole log redacted for PII.
- Data residency note: diagram and brief describing how EU tenant data is pinned to eu-west-1 and how we prevent cross-region restores.

Logistics:
- Delivery: secure ShareFile link (we'll send the link in the final email).
- Follow-up: propose Aug 31 09:00 PT for a 45 minute demo + Q&A (we can shift if that's not good for EU participants).

Anything else to add to the pack? If procurement needs formal language, Samir — please flag the specific contract clauses so Lauren's team can prepare a draft.

— Marissa Cole
Customer Security Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finpulse.com>, Samir Nair <snair@finpulse.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence pack and next steps for procurement (FP-2027-09)

Hi Olivia / Samir — delivering the promised artifacts. See secure bundle at the link below; attachments listed are samples and redacted examples for evaluation. All files in the bundle are copies with sensitive fields redacted.

Secure delivery: https://sharefile.redwood.com/s/evidence-pack-FP-2027-09
Delivered items (samples / redacted):
- iam-assume-role-example.json (text/json) — includes a RoleTrust policy, inline policy limiting S3 operations to customer prefix, and a sessionDurationSeconds example.
- breakglass-log-sample.txt (text/plain) — redacted CloudTrail-like entry showing AssumeRole, approver metadata, and a timestamp.
- cloudtrail-retention-screenshot.png (image/png) — UI screenshot showing retention set to 365 days and export job configuration.
- redwood-support-perms-matrix-v1.pdf (application/pdf) — same matrix from the call with role definitions and typical session lengths.

Notes / commitments:
- Session duration: routine support sessions will default to 4 hours; escalation sessions can be extended to 8 hours with explicit manager + on-call security approval.
- Notifications: break-glass triggers an automated email to the customer security contact and generates an incident ticket internally.
- Data exports: for EU-resident customer exports we require documented customer approval; export flow will be performed from eu-west-1 and logged.

Samir — if you want a draft contract addendum covering export approvals and SLAs, I can circulate by EOD Aug 26.

Thanks — feel free to reply with any follow-ups and we'll adjust the pack.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Security Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
-- End of thread --
